title: WPSS/265/2019 of SATISH CHANDRA JAKHMOLA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 265 of 2019 (S/S)
Satish Chandra Jakhmola .....Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and another ....Respondents
Mr. K.K. Harbola, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Addl. C.S.C. for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Bhupendra Singh Bisht, Advocate holding brief of Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate for
respondent No. 2 / Nigam.

Dated: 7th February, 2019
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The petitioner, who was working with the respondent,
had retired as Administrative Officer Grade-2 from the service on
30th April, 2014. In the writ petition, the petitioner has prayed for the
payment of retiral benefits as detailed in para 7 of the writ petition.
2. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is
that despite of the sanction being granted by virtue of the order dated
5th December, 2014, when the retiral dues were not paid, the
petitioner had submitted representation dated 10th August, 2018
before the authority concerned, but still, the grievance of the petitioner
remained un-redressed, which has resulted into filing of the present
Writ petition. Details of post retiral dues, as claimed by the petitioner
in para 7 of the writ petition, read as under:
A Commutation Rs.4,24,974/- (approx.)
(sanctioned but not paid)
B Arrears of Dearness
Allowances
Rs. 2493/- (approx)
(sanctioned but not paid)
C Arrears of Dearness
Allowances
Rs. 2780/- (approx)
(sanctioned but not paid)
D Arrears of 7th Pay
Commission (w.e.f 01.-01-
2016 to 31-12-2016)
-
Total Amount Rs. 4,61,498/- (Excluding
the amount of arrears of 7th
Pay Commission due w.e.f.
01.01.2016 to 31.12.2016)"

2
3. For the aforesaid reliefs, the petitioner claims parity
based on the judgment rendered in an identical Writ Petition, being
Writ Petition No. 2905 (S/S) of 2018, Maya Ram Vs. State of
Uttarakhand and another as decided by this Court on 21st
August, 2018 as well as judgment rendered by the Division Bench
in Writ Petition (S/B) No. 494 of 2015, Lalita Prasad Tewari
Vs. Uttarakhand Payjal Sansadhan Vikas Evam Nirman
Nigam, decided on 30th November, 2015 and also on the
judgement rendered in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 73 of 2019, Kailash
Chandra Naudiyal Vs. State of Uttarakhand and others on
10.01.2019 (Annexure No. 4 to the writ petition).
4. In view of the above, a writ of mandamus is issued to
the respondent Nigam directing it to pay the post retiral dues as
explained in para 7 of the writ petition, in the manner, as
stipulated hereunder :-
A Commutation Rs.4,24,974/- (approx.)
(sanctioned but not paid)
(within two months)
B Arrears of Dearness
Allowances
Rs. 2493/- (approx)
(sanctioned but not paid)
(within two months)
C Arrears of Dearness
Allowances
Rs. 2780/- (approx)
(sanctioned but not paid)
(within two months)
D Arrears of 7th Pay
Commission (w.e.f 01.-01-
2016 to 31-12-2016)
-
Total Amount Rs. 4,61,498/- (Excluding
the amount of arrears of 7th
Pay Commission due w.e.f.
01.01.2016 to 31.12.2016)
5. The respondents / Nigam is directed to pay the post
retiral dues to the petitioner as mentioned in paragraph No. 4 of the
judgment within a period as mentioned against each head of dues
payable to the petitioner from the date of presentation of the
certified copy of the judgment.
6. So far claim for payment of 7th Pay Commission is
concerned, the same is to be covered by the directions as issued by

3
the Division Bench in a judgment rendered in Writ Petition (S/B)
No. 639 of 2018, Shivraj Verma Vs. State of Uttarakhand and
another, as decided on 14th December, 2018.
7. Subject to the above observations, the writ petition
stands disposed of.
8. However, there would be no order as to costs.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Vacation Judge
 07.02.2019
Mahinder/
